item.title: Warriors center Charles Bassey decries Marcus Smart's attempted punch as ‘fake toughness'
item.description: Houston Rockets guard Marcus Smart, center, is held back after a confrontation with Golden State Warriors center Charles Bassey, left, during the second half of Wednesday's game in Houston. (Ashley Landis/Associated Press) HOUSTON - A half hour after the Punch That Didn't Land, Charles Bassey strolled back into the Golden State Warriors locker room, repeating the same two words that are in rapid danger of becoming his catchphrase. "Fake toughness," Bassey proclaimed. "Fake toughness." For all intents and purposes, however, this was real toughness, on Wednesday night. Late in the third quarter of a hotly-contested matchup between two longtime Western Conference foes - a matchup already crackling with the tension of Stephen Curry 's first-quarter injury - Houston guard Marcus Smart and Bassey became entangled and exchanged words near midcourt. The recollections of what happened thereafter vary slightly, depending on which side you asked. "He said, ‘Hey, don't do that,'" Bassey said, after Houston's 115-108 win over Golden State. "I'm like, ‘Do what? It's a grown man's league.'" Smart "said they got wrapped up," Rockets coach Ime Udoka said in a postgame press conference, as multiple Houston reporters shared. "And his elbow, that he had hurt, got bent up. And so he said something to him. And Bassey said, ‘What are you going to do?' And he did it." Well, not exactly. From nowhere came a punch. A right jab, to be specific. Bassey ducked his head, just so that Smart's hand caught nothing but air. A cohort of Warriors, led by rookie Yaxel Lendeborg, quickly intervened to pull Smart away. And the 32-year-old Smart headed for the locker room before referees even had the chance to eject him, which they did, of course. Bassey, a reserve center who has infused the Warriors' bench units with life, decried the whole incident postgame. Fake toughness. Smart was "playing dirty the whole game," Bassey said, and alleged the guard grabbed his knee and hand earlier in the night. "I knew he was gonna do something," Bassey said. "I baited for him to do something, because I knew he was going to do something. I don't think he was trying to play. I think he was trying to get himself out of the game. He wasn't trying to play … I think he was trying to chill. He wasn't trying to hoop, bro." There is a pattern forming, here, win or loss. Draymond Green, Golden State's emotional ringleader, repeated "I don't know" when asked why these Warriors continue to find themselves in a bevy of early-season skirmishes. Reason or not, they continue to add up. There has been Green's takedown of Suns big Khaman Maluach, and Georges Niang's noggin-to-noggin barking, and technicals for rookie Yaxel Lendeborg. Lendeborg, on a recent online stream, declared these Warriors the "remodeled Bad Boy Pistons" and predicted at least "10 more ejections" in Golden State's future. item.title: Ten years, three kids later - Oliva back for Olympic bid
item.description: Oliva (second from left) won Commonwealth bronze for Team Wales as part of the women's team pursuit in Glasgow [Getty Images] Cyclist and mum-of-three Ciara Oliva says she has 'unfinished business' at the Olympics after making a remarkable return to the British Cycling programme. The former European champion and world bronze medallist spent almost a decade out of the sport and has three children with partner and fellow cyclist, Lewis. But after missing out on final selection to compete at the Rio 2016 Games, the 37-year-old admits she just could not give up on her Olympic dream. She returned to international competition at the summer's Commonwealth Games, winning bronze for Wales in the women's team pursuit, but says that was only the start. "I could have stopped there," she told BBC Sport Wales. "It felt like one of the most magical moments. My favourite medal I've ever had internationally, winning a bronze medal with the girls in the team pursuit in front of my children. It was like a fairytale ending in itself. "But there's unfinished business and I am going to chase my Olympic dream one last time." Horne's Rio dream inspired by scrapbook Olympic heartache fuels Oliva's comeback Oliva first joined the Great Britain cycling programme in 2014. She won bronze at the 2016 World Championships as part of the women's team pursuit. She also won two European titles in the same event. But come the Rio 2016 Olympics, Oliva was left watching on as reserve. Laura Kenny, Katie Archibald, Elinor Barker and Joanna Rowsell were chosen for the Olympic team pursuit - and they smashed the world record to take gold. "The fastest team rode," she is happy to admit. "They won gold. "But I had to stand on the sidelines and watch that happen. And I was truly heartbroken." Oliva retired in 2018 and went on to be a physiotherapist, feeling "I honestly thought I was done". "People would mention cycling and I would discuss it, but I always found it hard to talk about the Olympics. I got so close and yet so far," she reflected. "The years went by and I had my three beautiful children, but I watched Helen Glover's documentary and I just burst into tears. I was like, I'm not done yet. "There was still that little voice that was saying, just have a crack at it one last time. "So to now have an opportunity to chase this, but this time with my family, my children by my side, watching mummy do all this crazy training day in day out, has just made the journey so much more special than I thought was even possible." item.title: Dan Campbell vs Mike Vrabel: A look back at when they faced off as players
item.description: When the Detroit Lions take on the New England Patriots in Germany on Sunday, Nov. 15, it will be a head-to-head matchup of former players for their respective teams. And about 20 years ago, they went head-to-head on the field. Let's take a little walk down memory lane, back to Dec. 3, 2006, when the 2-9 Lions traveled to face the 9-2 Patriots looking to play spoilers down the stretch. They were surprisingly in the game late into the fourth quarter and had the ball with a 21-all tie and about 8:30 to go in the game. That's when Dan Campbell, playing tight end in those days, made his lone catch of the day, a 21-yard down the seam. He popped up and showed off that trademark Campbell energy with a boisterous fist pump. On the next play, though, Mike Vrabel picked off Lions quarterback Jon Kitna. It proved costly, as the Patriots survived, 28-21. The play before Vrabel's INT, Dan Campbell caught a 21-yard pass on him, despite Vrabel re-routing him up the seam. It was Campbell's only catch that day. The Pats won 28-21. https://t.co/XAe2gC4Dj0 pic.twitter.com/OIR6Li7VXk — Andrew Callahan (@_AndrewCallahan) November 11, 2026 Campbell and Vrabel won't be thumping shoulder pads in this one, but they'll still face off in a game that's important to both teams. The Lions, of course, are trying to keep pace in the highly competitive NFC North at 6-2, while the Patriots are in danger of seeing their season spiral after a shellacking from the Green Bay Packers sent them to 5-4. item.title: Today in Boston Celtics history: Rick Robey extended; Andre Turner debuts
item.description: Today in Boston Celtics history, Frederick Robert Robey – better known to fans of the storied franchise as Rick – extended his contract with the team for several additional years. Robey became part of Boston's roster in January 1979, dealt to Boston by the Indiana Pacers for forward Billy Knight, and up to that moment of his career in the NBA, he had been something of an iron man, having missed a mere two contests in total suiting up for the Celtics. An alum of the University of Kentucky, Robey was picked up by the Pacers with the third overall pick of the 1978 NBA Draft, the sole ball club in the Association that he had played for before joining the Celtics. The Celtics eventually traded the Coral Gables native to the Phoenix Suns for legendary Boston point guard Dennis Johnson and draft assets, having averaged 8.3 points, 5.0 rebounds, and 1.3 assists per game with the team. Historic milestones It was also on this day in 1986 that former Celtics point guard Andre Turner played his first game for the team. Turner's debut with the team came in a 124-116 win over the Milwaukee Bucks at the old Boston Garden and saw the Memphis product log 2 points, a rebound, and an assist in 11 minutes of play. item.title: Why Pochettino’s USMNT Exit Might Be Good For US Soccer
item.description: ST. PAUL, MN - OCTOBER 6: Mauricio Pochettino, Head Coach of the USA and Jesse Marsch, Head Coach of Canada congratulate one another after the match during a game between Canada and United States at Allianz Field on October 6, 2026 in St. Paul, Minnesota. (Photo by Robin Alam/ISI Photos/ISI Photos via Getty Images) ISI Photos via Getty Images On the surface, Mauricio Pochettino’s likely departure from the U.S. men’s national team to take over as Manchester United’s manager might feel like a brutal blow. It wasn’t just that Pochettino led the USMNT to the round of 16 in the 2026 World Cup, but the perceived style with which that group played. It was considered a minor coup when U.S. Soccer convinced the Argentine to sign a new deal for the 2030 cycle, and the vibes got even better when a youthful U.S. group won all four of its friendlies in September and October. That he leaves so soon into his new deal feels like a bit of betrayal as well as a brutal indictment of U.S. Soccer’s place in the men’s global soccer hierarchy. Take away the emotion, though, and it might actually be the best possible outcome for the federation. That’s especially if you believe extending Pochettino in the first place wasn’t actually warranted based on results alone. Pochettino’s World Cup Popularity From a public relations standpoint, Pochettino’s USMNT was enormously successful. The Yanks played some decidedly stylish stuff, particularly in the opening match against Paraguay , in the first half of the second match against Australia, and in the round of 32 against Bosnia and Herzegovina. Unprecedented pro-U.S. crowds turned up to stadiums, tuned in on TV and liked what they saw, except for a 4-1 loss to Belgium in the round of 16. The majority of the fanbase clearly wanted Pochettino to stay, believing the quality of play had improved. And it was true that the team played more cohesively than earlier during Pochettino’s tenure, when he clearly used friendlies and even competitive Concacaf matches to evaluate talent first and earn results second. Fooled By The World Cup Format? However, this enthusiasm didn’t reflect the competitive facts. Rather, the expectations for the program became so low at the end of previous manager Gregg Berhalter’s tenure that a historically average World Cup performance was celebrated as something more. The expanded tournament format and favorable seeding skewed this perception. Casual fans only saw World Cup performances that were more dominant than in previous tournaments. They neglected the reality that the USMNT played four opponents in 2026 ranked lower in the FIFA World Rankings than any of their four foes in 2022. Ultimately, they exited at the same stage. And the loss to Belgium represented the largest margin of defeat in a U.S. World Cup knockout match since a 6-1 defeat to Argentina in the 1930 semifinals. Adding to the difficulty, for both teams, is that the game will take play overseas: the Patriots and Lions will face off in Munich, Germany, as part of the NFL’s International Series. item.description: Thomas Sparks was arrested after he allegedly choked a youth basketball referee in Shelton, police said. He is due back in court Thursday. (Courtesy of Shelton Police Department ) DERBY- A former Westport high school girls basketball coach will face a judge today on charges he choked and assaulted a referee at a youth basketball game in Shelton last month. Thomas Sparks, 37, was arrested Oct. 24 and charged with third-degree assault, second-degree strangulation and risk of injury to a child after a referee at a youth basketball game at the Boys and Girls Club in Shelton filed a complaint, a police report said. Sparks was released on $10,000 bond and is due back in state Superior Court in Derby Thursday. Sparks resigned as the Staples High School girls basketball coach in late October after leading the team since 2024. "Tommy resigned for personal and family considerations," Staples High School Athletic Director VJ Sarullo said at the time. Sparks was coaching a team for the Connecticut Elite youth basketball league on Oct. 24 when he confronted the referee about what he perceived to be a bad foul call, the police report said. Officials at Connecticut Elite declined to discuss the incident a few weeks ago, but said Sparks no longer works for them. During a verbal exchange, the referee told police that Sparks called him an expletive and then seconds later tripped and shoved him to the ground, according to the report. Before the referee could get up, Sparks put his arm around the man's neck, at which point others in the crowd stepped in to intervene, the police report said. Sparks was ejected from the building, and the referee later went to the police station to file a report. He told police that he felt like he might pass out while Sparks had his arm was around his neck, the report said. Sparks told police that he took physical action because he didn't know what the referee would do after their verbal exchange, the report said. Witnesses, including some of the players, confirmed the referee's version of events, police said. Sparks was hired by Westport schools in 2024 to coach the varsity girls basketball team. After Wednesday’s practice, Hinzman admitted the losses have exposed problems that might otherwise have gone unnoticed. “When everything’s going well, I think it’s easy to look over some of the flaws you have. And so we have that energy and that juice in the silence as well, which is gonna be huge.” Urban Meyer Calls Out Ohio State’s Quarterback Decisions Amid Losing Streak Former Ohio State head coach Urban Meyer has raised questions about Ryan Day’s handling of the quarterback situation. It’s led to Andoni Iraola deploying the on-loan Ronald Araujo – conventionally a centre-back – on the right-hand side of defence, and thankfully the Uruguayan has been a sturdy presence in the Reds’ back four so far this season. Nearly a year on from agreeing a deal to sign Jacquet, Liverpool could once more turn to Ligue 1 for a breakthrough defensive prospect. Liverpool monitoring Djibril Ouziad According to Get French Football News , the Reds are currently monitoring Le Havre right-back Djibril Ouziad, who’s also being watched by Aston Villa. The 17-year-old signed his first professional contract at the Stade Oceane in September, penning terms until 2030, but he’s deemed ‘likely to leave’ next summer even if his current club pull themselves out of the relegation zone in the French top flight. item.description: Pep Guardiola could be set to return to management after latest update Pep Guardiola and USMNT: Why a Stunning International Move Is Now Being Considered US Soccer are exploring one of the biggest managerial appointments the international game could offer, with talkSPORT reporting that Pep Guardiola is wanted as the next USMNT head coach. It is a development that would reshape the market quickly, particularly with Mauricio Pochettino seemingly moving towards Manchester United after agreeing a deal in principle to replace Michael Carrick. For the United States, the attraction is obvious. Guardiola has been out of management since leaving Manchester City in the summer, ending a decade in which he collected six Premier League titles and the Champions League. Add in his league success at Barcelona and Bayern Munich, and the profile is unmatched. If US Soccer can even bring him into serious discussions, it becomes a statement of intent before a hugely important period for the national side. Photo IMAGO USMNT job offers fresh challenge One detail stands out immediately. Guardiola has never managed in international football. That makes the USMNT role a genuinely new test for a coach who has already conquered the club game across multiple countries. There is clear logic in the idea that a national team post, with a different rhythm and shorter windows of work, might appeal at some stage. Yet there is an equally important complication. Guardiola has been very clear about his desire to step away. In May 2025, he said: “After my contract with City, I’m going to stop. I’m sure.” He added: “I don’t know if I’m going to retire, but I’m going to take a break. How I want to be remembered, I don’t know.” Pep Guardiola break remains key factor That theme has remained consistent. In another interview, Guardiola reiterated: “So I’m not retiring, but I will take a break, for sure.” He also said: “When I finish here, I will take a break. I need to make a stop, that’s all.” Those are strong words, and anyone pursuing him will need to assess whether enough time has passed for his stance to soften. He has still stayed close to Manchester City from afar. After the club were found guilty on all charges of Premier League financial breaches in September, Guardiola told supporters: “Let me be clear: we will get through this together. I love you all.” He was also present for City’s 4-2 home defeat to Paris Saint-Germain last month. Gold Cup timeline could accelerate decision If the USMNT are serious, timing matters. The Gold Cup next summer offers a natural starting point, and that may explain the urgency around the process. Much will depend on Guardiola’s appetite to return now, rather than later. For US Soccer, however, even attempting this dramatic swoop shows the scale of their ambition. Source: talkSPORT

item.description: Serena Williams | © Imagn Coco Gauff’s father, Corey Gauff, has called out a social media post highlighting the endorsement deals of tennis legends Serena Williams, Venus Williams, Maria Sharapova, and other female athletes. An Instagram post shared by Athlete listed what it described as the 10 biggest female contracts in sports. It included several high-profile deals involving tennis players, beginning with Venus Williams’ reported $40 million agreement with Reebok in 2000. The post stated that Reebok re-signed Venus to a five-year deal in December 2000, which was reportedly the richest contract ever given to a female athlete at the time. It then mentioned Serena Williams’ Nike deal, claiming the company signed her away from Puma in December 2002 on a five-year contract with a three-year option. The post also referred to performance bonuses for winning Grand Slam titles or finishing the year as World No. 1. Another deal highlighted was Maria Sharapova’s reported $70 million Nike contract. In 2010, the Russian signed an eight-year extension that included her own dress collection and a percentage of sales. The post caught the attention of Corey, who disputed the information shared by the page. I’ve been with Nike for over 15 years, and I’ve been able to see the ins and outs of how to successfully run such a great consumer brands company,” said Serena Williams. She also praised the company’s willingness to stand by its beliefs and values. “Nike is one of those brands out there that [is] not going to be afraid to say how they feel and to stand up for what they feel is right. item.description: Arsenal v Tottenham Hotspur - Carabao Cup: Quarter Final - Getty Images Sport Manchester United are rapidly closing in on the appointment of Mauricio Pochettino, but reports suggest the dressing room had other ideas for the top job. While the former Tottenham and Chelsea boss is the man chosen to lead the rebuild, a significant portion of the squad was reportedly holding out for a different Premier League rival. United close on Pochettino as Carrick faces axe Manchester United currently sit in the Premier League relegation zone, marking their worst start to a domestic campaign in 40 years. With senior club figures gathering in Monaco to determine a path forward, Michael Carrick is expected to pay the price for the disastrous run of form. Pochettino has emerged as the clear frontrunner to take charge . The Red Devils have already reached an agreement to release the Argentine from his newly signed contract with the United States national team, clearing the way for his imminent arrival at Old Trafford. Dressing room preference for Villa boss Despite the impending managerial change, talkSPORT reports that a number of the United squad wanted Unai Emery to take the reins. The Spaniard was heavily linked with the vacancy, and his remarkable transformation of Aston Villa has made him a popular choice among the players. Emery has cemented his elite status by guiding Villa to Champions League qualification twice and delivering a Europa League crown last season. He has achieved this sustained success while balancing the club's finances and coping with high-profile summer departures. Prior triumphs at Sevilla, Villarreal, and Valencia have further boosted his formidable reputation. Contrasting Premier League track records Emery recently experienced a frustrating visit to Old Trafford on Sunday. His Villa side surrendered a two-goal advantage twice in a thrilling 4-4 draw , prompting the furious manager to storm down the tunnel before the final whistle. While his stock remains incredibly high, underwhelming past stints under the immense pressure of Arsenal and Paris Saint-Germain remain the only blemishes on his managerial record. Meanwhile, Pochettino returns to English football following a brief one-year spell at Chelsea, where he secured a sixth-place finish. His greatest Premier League achievements came at Tottenham, leading the London club to consecutive top-three finishes. That success previously made him a prime candidate for the United job in 2018 before Ole Gunnar Solskjaer was ultimately appointed. Immediate task for the incoming manager Pochettino will inherit a fractured team languishing at the wrong end of the table. His immediate priority must be dragging United out of the relegation zone and unifying a dressing room that seemingly favoured another candidate. Overcoming the initial scepticism of the squad will be crucial as he attempts to salvage a campaign that is rapidly spiralling out of control.

item.title: ‘That’s enough’ – Skip Bayless slams JJ Redick for not trying to ‘save’ Luka Doncic from himself
item.description: Photo by Patrick McDermott/Getty Images Luka Doncic suffered an injury scare against the Milwaukee Bucks, and Skip Bayless believes JJ Redick is to blame. Luka Doncic seemed to injure his ankle due to a dangerous closeout from Kyle Kuzma in the fourth quarter of a blowout win for the Los Angeles Lakers. Both players would end up leaving the game after getting hurt, but the Los Angeles Lakers still managed to earn a big win to extend their record to 11-2. Skip Bayless questions JJ Redick not managing Luka Doncic’s minutes amid injury scare Taking to X following the Los Angeles Lakers’ win against the Milwaukee Bucks, Skip Bayless criticised JJ Redick for not taking Luka Doncic out of the game before he injured his ankle. He suggested that the Lakers were well on their way to a victory, and Redick should have ignored Doncic’s desire to score 30 points in order to avoid the injury scare. Bayless wrote: “No idea why Luka was still in this blowout – just turned his ankle with AR already gone due to heel injury. I realise Luka wanted to at least get his 30 – he wound up with 32 – but JJ has to save Luka from himself and say that’s enough.” Bayless does make a valid point here. The Lakers had a significant lead at that point, and the Bucks were not making any efforts to mount a comeback. While Doncic wanting to stay in the game and score 30 points is understandable, given that he had a rare poor shooting night and wanted to keep his streak of scoring 30+ points a game going, it was a risk that didn’t need to be taken. Last season, Doncic missed a significant portion of the regular season and the Lakers’ entire playoff run due to an injury he sustained against the Oklahoma City Thunder. There has been concern about Doncic’s fitness and health since he joined the Lakers. Even though he has looked much healthier coming into this season, injuries can occur at any time, and the Lakers didn’t need to take such an unnecessary risk with Doncic just to satisfy his desire to keep his individual numbers strong. Thankfully, the injury doesn’t appear to be serious, although more will be revealed tomorrow when the Lakers can conduct tests on Doncic’s ankle.
